placements.why: The envelope's content is fundamentally about calibrating and verifying an instrument — an organizational category of work that nothing in the existing (empty) strata covers. Calibration is named in the org's strata taxonomy as a recognized category, and this envelope's content calls for it to be minted.
placements.title: Instrument calibration as a verifiable organizational practice
placements.theme: Calibration establishes and verifies instrument readiness against reference standards before observation.

placements.title: Calibration holds across the full observing band when verified against reference plates
placements.theme: Instrument calibration is established at a target frequency and verified against reference standards to confirm it holds across the operating range.
placements.why: All three segments cohere around a single thematic subject: the Kestrelwood spectrograph is calibrated at 88.4 MHz and that calibration is verified against June reference plates, holding across the full observing band. src-2 names the instrument, src-3 specifies the calibration parameters and reference, and src-1 asserts the verified result. This is a thematic container future envelopes about calibration verification can feed — not a one-time fact, but a recurring subject of instrument readiness.
